question: Does a published fixed monthly trend rule improve drawdown and losing-month frequency beyond a calibration-only fixed equity allocation?
data_route: Reuse existing SPY adjusted-price snapshot; download public issuer BIL NAV and historical distributions once per file. Prior Yahoo429 and next-open experiment remain preserved as incomplete.
model: Separately frozen same-close idealized mixed market-total-return/NAV exercise; fixed SMA10, calibration-only q, four fixed comparisons and unchanged163-month test. No parameter scan or new trading framework.
corporate_action: Issuer-authored announcement and SEC record corroborate BIL2017-11-30 reverse split. Apply half as many shares once; do not mistake raw NAV doubling for profit.
conditional_input: Historical distribution amounts interpreted as contemporaneous per-share amounts; no retrospective re-scaling. Full historical convention not certified; retained auxiliary source contradictions do not enter the selected return fields.

independent_acceptance.blindness_limit: Calibrationq was shared before executor run; full curves/metrics were not. Not a fully blind experiment.

source_crosscheck: Seven available issuer NAV period-return comparisons agree within the published rounding unit; narrow source consistency check, not all-data certification.
interpretation: A mixed economic tradeoff was observed. This study does not establish an implementable timing edge or a funded strategy; retain result and proceed by evidence rather than tuning. Numeric strategy performance remains private.
model_collaboration: Codex independent method critic, executor and numerical verifier completed scoped work. Current official DeepSeek request timed out without final; old WorkBuddy request remainedThinking. Neither missing final counts as a critique.
publication_scope: Methods, public source links and evidence hashes/status only. No raw vendor series, numeric private strategy performance, credentials, account material, personal paths or conversations.
